rubrics.justification: Generally consistent with a good-quality expanded blastocyst and the provided 3AA grade, but it overstates certainty from a single image, including speculative early hatching/focal herniation and a very confident AA-level ICM/TE description despite limited visual clarity and somewhat indistinct TE/ICM in the image.
Thoroughly integrates age, AMH/ovarian reserve, BMI, male factor, prior live birth, endometrium, and lifestyle with embryo quality and prognosis, highlighting both favorable and limiting factors.

Reasoning is structured and mostly logical, with a clear link from morphology and patient factors to prognosis; minor issues include somewhat confident quantitative adjustments and assumptions about euploidy/implantation rates.

Mostly aligned on SET, blastocyst assessment, and general counseling, but includes several recommendations that are more controversial or not guideline-standard (routine PGT-A framing in low-yield cases, DHEA/GH, acupuncture, progesterone monitoring rationale tied to low BMI).

Provides clear next-step recommendations for transfer management and future cycle planning, including SET, luteal support, repeat-cycle strategy, and male-factor workup; some suggestions are less evidence-based but still practical.
